pinyin: yī dài gèng bǐ yī dài qiáng
literal: one · generation · even more than · one · generation · strong
natural: each generation is stronger than the last

meaning.en: Each generation surpasses the one before it.
meaning.zh: 每一代人都比上一代人更出色。

equivalents: the new generation is better than the old

examples.zh: 看到年轻运动员的表现，大家都说一代更比一代强。
examples.en: Watching the young athletes, everyone said each generation is better than the last.

examples.zh: 我们这一代已经不错了，可孩子们真是一代更比一代强。
examples.en: Our generation did well enough, but the kids are really better still.

usage.en: Praise for the young, often in sport, science and the arts. Casual; a full sentence.
usage.zh: 多用于称赞年轻人，常见于体育、科研、艺术等领域。口语，常单独成句。

literal: good to · look at · not · good to · use
natural: nice to look at but no use

meaning.en: Attractive on the outside but useless in practice.
meaning.zh: 外表好看，实际不好用，没有实用价值。

examples.zh: 这套花哨的家具中看不中用，坐着一点也不舒服。
examples.en: This fancy furniture is all looks and no use; it isn't comfortable at all.

examples.zh: 选手机不能只看外观，免得买到中看不中用的。
examples.en: Don't choose a phone by its looks alone, or you will end up with one that is pretty but useless.

usage.en: Used of things and, jokingly, of people. Note 中 is read zhōng here. Casual; predicate or attributive.
usage.zh: 可指物，也可戏指人。此处“中”读 zhōng。口语，作谓语、定语。

meaning.en: Describes a person so cruel that he kills without a flicker of hesitation.
meaning.zh: 形容人极其凶狠残忍，杀人时眼睛都不眨一下。

examples.zh: 这伙匪徒杀人不眨眼，村里人都不敢出门。
examples.en: The bandits were cold-blooded killers, and the villagers dared not go out.

examples.zh: 他看上去斯文，其实是个杀人不眨眼的恶魔。
examples.en: He looks refined, but he is in fact a ruthless killer.

usage.en: Used as an attributive (杀人不眨眼的魔王) or predicate; casual and vivid. Often exaggerated.
usage.zh: 多作定语（杀人不眨眼的魔王）或谓语，口语，形象夸张。

natural: let water in to raise fish

meaning.en: To nurture the source of future gain rather than draining it, for example by easing burdens so that people and businesses can grow.
meaning.zh: 比喻着眼长远，先培养财源、减轻负担，让对方得到发展。

equivalents: nurture the goose that lays the golden eggs

examples.zh: 政府减税让利，是为了放水养鱼，扶持小企业成长。
examples.en: The government cut taxes to nurture small businesses so that they can grow.

examples.zh: 做生意要放水养鱼，不能只盯着眼前的利润。
examples.en: In business you have to nurture your customers, not just chase the profit in front of you.

usage.en: Mostly policy and business talk, set against 竭泽而渔. Neutral to positive.
usage.zh: 多见于政策和商业语境，与“竭泽而渔”相对。中性偏褒。

meaning.en: A person who works or fights with all-out, almost reckless energy.
meaning.zh: 指干事不要命、拼尽全力的人。

examples.zh: 他是公司里有名的拼命三郎，常常工作到半夜。
examples.en: He is known at the company as a workaholic who often works until midnight.

examples.zh: 球队里这位拼命三郎，每场都跑得最多。
examples.en: The team's all-out player runs more than anyone else in every match.

story.en: In the novel Water Margin, the Liangshan outlaw Shi Xiu is nicknamed 拼命三郎 ('Desperate Third Brother') for fighting with no thought for his own life.
story.zh: 《水浒传》中，梁山好汉石秀因作战不顾性命，绰号“拼命三郎”。

usage.en: Used as a nickname or praise, sometimes with a note of worry about overwork. Casual; object or predicate.
usage.zh: 可作绰号或赞语，有时也含对过度劳累的担忧。口语，作宾语、谓语。

natural: eat fragrant food and drink hot spirits

meaning.en: To live well, with plenty of good food and drink.
meaning.zh: 形容生活富足，有吃有喝，过得好。

examples.zh: 跟着这个老板干，大家都能吃香喝辣。
examples.en: If you work for this boss, everyone gets to live well.

examples.zh: 他在外面吃香喝辣，家里人却一无所知。
examples.en: He ate and drank well outside, while his family knew nothing about it.

usage.en: Casual, often about prosperity or an enviable life; can be slightly teasing. Do not confuse with 吃香, 'be popular'.
usage.zh: 口语，多指生活富足，有时带调侃。不要与“吃香”（受欢迎）相混。

pinyin: qī dà gū bā dà yí
literal: seven · big · paternal aunt · eight · big · maternal aunt
natural: seven great aunts and eight great aunties

meaning.en: A humorous way of saying 'all one's relatives', especially the many distant ones on both sides of the family.
meaning.zh: 泛指众多亲戚，尤其是父母两边各种远近亲戚，带幽默意味。

equivalents: every aunt and uncle in the family

examples.zh: 春节回老家，七大姑八大姨都来问我有没有对象。
examples.en: When I went home for the New Year, all my aunts and relatives asked whether I had a partner.

examples.zh: 婚礼上来了七大姑八大姨，热闹极了。
examples.en: All the relatives turned up at the wedding, and it was very lively.

usage.en: Typical of New Year chatter about being nosy relatives. Casual and humorous; object or subject.
usage.zh: 常出现在春节话题里，调侃爱打听的亲戚。口语、诙谐，作主语、宾语。

meaning.en: Words that go round and round, repeating the same thing over and over like a rolling wheel.
meaning.zh: 像车轮一样转来转去、翻来覆去说的话。

equivalents: say the same thing over and over

examples.zh: 他说来说去都是车轱辘话，一点新意也没有。
examples.en: He kept saying the same things over and over without anything new.

examples.zh: 会上有人反复说车轱辘话，大家都听烦了。
examples.en: Someone at the meeting kept going round in circles, and everyone got fed up.

usage.en: Usually 说车轱辘话 or 车轱辘话来回说. Casual, a little rude; the 辘 is neutral-toned in speech (gū lu).
usage.zh: 常说“说车轱辘话”“车轱辘话来回说”。口语，略带不耐烦；口语中“辘”读轻声（gū lu）。

natural: an obsession with office clouding the mind

meaning.en: So obsessed with rank and promotion that one has lost all judgement.
meaning.zh: 一心想做官、升官，被官位迷住了头脑，失去理智。

examples.zh: 他官迷心窍，为了升职什么都肯干。
examples.en: He is so obsessed with rank that he would do anything to be promoted.

examples.zh: 别官迷心窍了，先把本职工作做好。
examples.en: Don't get so hung up on promotion; do your own job well first.

usage.en: Mocks careerism, often in a casual, jeering tone. Predicate.
usage.zh: 讽刺热衷升官的人，口语，带嘲讽。作谓语。

antonyms: 青年要立志做大事，不可立志做大官

meaning.en: To see spots of light before the eyes, usually from dizziness, a blow or standing up too fast.
meaning.zh: 因头晕、撞击或猛然站起而眼前出现闪光的小点。

examples.zh: 我一下子站起来，顿时眼冒金星。
examples.en: I stood up all at once and immediately saw stars.

examples.zh: 被球砸中脑袋，他疼得眼冒金星。
examples.en: Hit on the head by the ball, he saw stars from the pain.

usage.zh: 可指实际感觉，也可夸张。口语。

natural: be generous with someone else's goods

meaning.en: To be generous at someone else's expense, spending or giving away what belongs to others.
meaning.zh: 拿别人的财物来做人情，自己慷慨，由别人付出代价。

equivalents: be generous with other people's money

examples.zh: 他慷他人之慨，用公司的钱请客，自己落了个好名声。
examples.en: He was generous with the company's money by treating people, and won a good name for himself.

examples.zh: 别慷他人之慨，这笔预算不归你支配。
examples.en: Don't be generous with other people's money; this budget is not yours to spend.

usage.en: Sarcastic; the original 慷慨 is split into 慷……之慨. Neutral register, written or spoken.
usage.zh: 带讽刺；把“慷慨”拆开用作“慷……之慨”。书面、口语均可。

meaning.en: Too many people competing for too little to go round.
meaning.zh: 比喻人多东西少，不够分。

examples.zh: 热门岗位狼多肉少，竞争特别激烈。
examples.en: Popular jobs have too many applicants for too few places, and competition is fierce.

examples.zh: 房源紧张，狼多肉少，租房得抓紧。
examples.en: Housing is tight, with too many people chasing too few flats, so you must rent quickly.

usage.en: Describes scarcity in jobs, housing and tickets. Casual; predicate.
usage.zh: 形容工作、住房、车票等紧缺。口语，作谓语。

meaning.en: Serious, proper and in earnest, often said with a hint of surprise or teasing.
meaning.zh: 认真、正式、规规矩矩，常带点意外或调侃。

examples.zh: 他今天穿得正儿八经，像要去面试。
examples.en: He is dressed very properly today, as if going to an interview.

examples.zh: 说点正儿八经的，你到底打算怎么办？
examples.en: Let's be serious for a moment: what exactly do you plan to do?

usage.en: Northern colloquial; used attributively (正儿八经的工作) or as adverb. 儿 is a suffix and is read er.
usage.zh: 北方口语，可作定语（正儿八经的工作）或状语。“儿”为词尾，读 er。

natural: serve different dishes according to who it is

meaning.en: To treat people differently according to their status or what one can get from them.
meaning.zh: 根据对方的身份地位、能否有好处来区别对待。

equivalents: be a snob to those below you

examples.zh: 这家店的服务员看人下菜碟，对穿得普通的客人爱答不理。
examples.en: The staff in this shop treat customers according to their looks and ignore those in ordinary clothes.

examples.zh: 做人不能看人下菜碟，对谁都该一样客气。
examples.en: You shouldn't treat people differently by status; be equally polite to everyone.

usage.en: Criticises snobbery and servility. Casual; predicate.
usage.zh: 批评势利、嫌贫爱富。口语，作谓语。

natural: swap a wildcat for the crown prince

meaning.en: To secretly substitute a fake for the real thing, especially to deceive on a major matter.
meaning.zh: 暗中用假的换掉真的，比喻玩弄手段欺骗。

examples.zh: 这批货被人狸猫换太子，客户收到的是次品。
examples.en: Someone secretly switched the goods, and the customer received an inferior product.

examples.zh: 他用旧零件狸猫换太子，被质检员当场识破。
examples.en: He swapped in old parts for the real ones, and the inspector saw through it on the spot.

story.en: In the Qing-dynasty novel 'Three Knights and Five Gallants', a rival concubine has the newborn prince stolen and replaced with a skinned wildcat to frame the empress; the story of Judge Bao later clears the empress.
story.zh: 清代小说《三侠五义》写宫中嫔妃用剥皮狸猫调换刚出生的太子，陷害皇后，后经包公查明冤情。

usage.en: Often used of fraud, forgery and switched goods. Casual; predicate or object.
usage.zh: 多用于调包、造假等欺骗行为。口语，作谓语、宾语。
